ratings.text:
See your misstep,
turn back early.
ratings.reasons: Passes the rules: 17 and 16 characters, 6 words, plain literal words, none of the banned words. Faithful: 'turn back early' is 不遠復 (returning from not far) and 'See your misstep' is the self-correction the Image commentary means by 以脩身也, the Xici's Yan Hui who always noticed his own fault and did not repeat it. It fixes round 4's gap: the misstep names what you turn back from, so it no longer reads as 'stay close to home', and it asks for an act of judgment (notice, then correct), not a forecast. A newcomer gets what Return asks: when you have gone wrong, come back to the path, and do it soon. Works with the picture: the bottom line breaking and its halves drifting apart and dimming is the misstep, the rejoin in an amber flash is the turn back, and 'turn back' sits under the rejoin. Distinct from the other eleven: no colon form (11, 12, 27), not 'step back' (15), and 'your misstep' separates it from 44's outside bad start and 51's self-examination under a shock. Why not 9: 'early' is not quite shown, since the halves hold apart for most of the act before rejoining, and the line leaves out the source's reward (無祇悔, no great regret; 元吉, supremely favourable), which would tell a viewer why early matters. Neither is worth another round; the line fits the space and says it plainly.
